description: Where time goes in Coder Agents chat turns, from the coderd_chatd_stage_duration_seconds stage histogram.

panels.description: How many coderd replicas report each --chat-stage-metrics level, from coderd_chatd_stage_metrics_level. The gauge has a series per level and only the configured one reads 1, so a replica restarted at a new level shows its new level on the next scrape. The visible rows work at basic; the collapsed rows need full. At off, every stage panel is empty.

targets.expr: count by (level) (coderd_chatd_stage_metrics_level == 1)

panels.title: Stage metrics level

panels.description:
Wall time of a whole chat turn, from the chat_turn stage, split by chat kind.

One sample per turn, so this is the top of the tree and the denominator every other level is measured against. Splitting by chat kind keeps slow subagent turns from hiding inside a blended line; the chat kind variable narrows which turns are counted. The model variable does not apply.

Mean is rate(_sum)/rate(_count); percentiles are histogram_quantile over the bucket rates. Idle chat kinds drop out instead of returning NaN.

targets.expr:
(
  histogram_quantile($stat, sum by (le, chat_kind) (rate(coderd_chatd_stage_duration_seconds_bucket{stage="chat_turn", chat_kind=~"$chat_kind", scope="turn"}[$__rate_interval])))
  and on() (vector($stat) > bool 0) == 1
  and on(chat_kind) (sum by (chat_kind) (rate(coderd_chatd_stage_duration_seconds_count{stage="chat_turn", chat_kind=~"$chat_kind", scope="turn"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)
)
or
(
  sum by (chat_kind) (rate(coderd_chatd_stage_duration_seconds_sum{stage="chat_turn", chat_kind=~"$chat_kind", scope="turn"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (chat_kind) (rate(coderd_chatd_stage_duration_seconds_count{stage="chat_turn", chat_kind=~"$chat_kind", scope="turn"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)
  and on() (vector($stat) == bool 0) == 1
)

panels.title: Turn duration (${stat:text})

panels.description:
Closed chat turns per minute, from the chat_turn sample count, split by chat kind. chat_turn is observed on every close, so every closed turn is counted whatever its outcome.

Read it next to turn duration: a duration change with flat throughput is a latency regression, while both moving together usually means the workload changed.

The chat kind variable applies. The model variable does not apply.

targets.expr: 60 * sum by (chat_kind) (rate(coderd_chatd_stage_duration_seconds_count{stage="chat_turn", chat_kind=~"$chat_kind", scope="turn"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Turns per minute

panels.description:
How turn wall time splits across the exclusive turn-time categories, per chat kind, over the dashboard time range. Each bar is one chat kind and sums to 100%; the value is that category's total seconds divided by all categories' total seconds, from increase() over the range.

The categories partition the turn, so unlike the stage panels they do not overlap and do add up. unattributed is the remainder the stage instrumentation could not place; watch it as the completeness check for the chat kind.

The chat kind variable applies. The model variable does not apply. Grouping is fixed to chat kind because Grafana transformation options do not interpolate dashboard variables.

targets.expr:
100 * sum by (chat_kind, category) (increase(coderd_chatd_turn_time_seconds_total{chat_kind=~"$chat_kind"}[$__range]))
/ on(chat_kind) group_left() (sum by (chat_kind) (increase(coderd_chatd_turn_time_seconds_total{chat_kind=~"$chat_kind"}[$__range])) > 0)

panels.title: Turn time mix by chat kind

panels.description:
Closed chat turns per minute by outcome, from coderd_chatd_turn_outcomes_total, stacked. Every closed turn is counted exactly once: completed turns finished normally and are the ones whose time partition is recorded; interrupted turns were cut off by a cancellation (a user interrupt or a shutdown); error turns stopped on any other failure; abandoned turns were closed before they finished without a failure or cancellation recorded against them. The stacked total equals Turns per minute.

The chat kind variable applies. The model variable does not apply.

targets.expr: 60 * sum by (outcome) (rate(coderd_chatd_turn_outcomes_total{chat_kind=~"$chat_kind"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Turn outcomes

panels.description:
Mean seconds per turn spent in each turn-time category, stacked, plus the total turn duration as a line. Each category's seconds from coderd_chatd_turn_time_seconds_total are divided by the turn count from coderd_chatd_turns_total, which counts each turn once when its partition is recorded.

Because the categories are exclusive, the stack height equals the mean turn duration and the line should sit on top of the stack. A gap between them means categories were dropped by the chat kind selection rather than by the partition.

Intervals with no completed turns are dropped instead of dividing by zero.

The chat kind variable applies. The model variable does not apply.

targets.expr:
sum by (category) (rate(coderd_chatd_turn_time_seconds_total{chat_kind=~"$chat_kind"}[$__rate_interval]))
/ on() group_left() (sum(rate(coderd_chatd_turns_total{chat_kind=~"$chat_kind"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

sum(rate(coderd_chatd_turn_time_seconds_total{chat_kind=~"$chat_kind"}[$__rate_interval]))
/ on() group_left() (sum(rate(coderd_chatd_turns_total{chat_kind=~"$chat_kind"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Seconds per turn by category

panels.description:
Turn time the stage instrumentation could not place in any category: mean unattributed seconds per turn.

This is the completeness check for the stage model. Near zero means the categories account for the turn. A rising line means real turn time is happening outside every instrumented stage, so the profile and partition panels are understating something; treat it as a bug in the instrumentation rather than as a workload change.

The chat kind variable applies. The model variable does not apply. The per-turn share distribution is in the collapsed row below.

targets.expr:
sum(rate(coderd_chatd_turn_time_seconds_total{category="unattributed", chat_kind=~"$chat_kind"}[$__rate_interval]))
/ (sum(rate(coderd_chatd_turns_total{chat_kind=~"$chat_kind"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)

panels.title: Unattributed turn time

panels.description:
Distribution of each category's share of a turn, from the coderd_chatd_turn_time_share histogram recorded once per turn. The statistic variable selects the statistic, so p99 reads as "in the worst turns, this category took this fraction of the turn".

Use it next to the mix bar: the bar shows where aggregate time goes, this shows how much a category varies per turn. A category with a small mean and a large p99 is bursty (a slow tool call or a retry storm in a minority of turns) rather than a steady cost.

Quantiles are per category, so unlike the mean shares they do not sum to 100%. The chat kind variable applies. The model variable does not apply.

targets.expr:
(
  histogram_quantile($stat, sum by (le, category) (rate(coderd_chatd_turn_time_share_bucket{chat_kind=~"$chat_kind"}[$__rate_interval])))
  and on() (vector($stat) > bool 0) == 1
  and on(category) (sum by (category) (rate(coderd_chatd_turn_time_share_count{chat_kind=~"$chat_kind"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)
)
or
(
  sum by (category) (rate(coderd_chatd_turn_time_share_sum{chat_kind=~"$chat_kind"}[$__rate_interval])) / (sum by (category) (rate(coderd_chatd_turn_time_share_count{chat_kind=~"$chat_kind"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0)
  and on() (vector($stat) == bool 0) == 1
)
